newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine gov't defends new phone rate structure.
newsitem.headline: Argentine gov't defends new phone rate structure.

text.p: Cabinet Chief Jorge Rodriguez tried to assure Argentina Thursday that the new telephone tariff structure would mean a tiny increase in phone bills for families but a big boost for small businesses.

He said there was "no way" the revised structure was what Telecom and Telefonica, who replaced state phone monopoly ENTEL in a 1991 privatization, had been lobbying for in long, drawn-out public audiences.
Telecom revealed earlier Thursday that the government had set reductions in long-distance call rates and increased some tariffs for local calls.
The companies had been lobbying for reduced long-distance call rates, arguing it would make charges fairer and reduce costs for businesses, especially in the provinces.
Consumer groups had argued on the other hand that private users' bills would rise because of increases in local call rates and phone companies would pocket the difference.
"The (increase) each family will pay will be insignificant because of the discounts in other types of calls," the Cabinet Chief told a news conference.

"But it will mean major relief for small and medium-sized industries and businesses in the interior of the country," he said. "It will mean a genera reduction of between 60-80 percent in the interior."
